### Findings (mechanism + impact + cheap falsification)

| # | Mechanism | Why it matters | Cheap deterministic check |
|---|-----------|----------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Stale-state race in `current_operational_state.json`** – 10‑min schedule + push‑based runs mutate the same JSON without file‑locking/atomic write. Later runs may read a partially written or prior‑run state, skipping gates or duplicating work. | Breaks reproducibility; creates silent duplicate‑work or premature gate advancement. | Write to `*.tmp` then `os.rename` (or `fcntl` lock on Linux, `LockFileEx` on Windows). Verify that two concurrent runs never observe the same `state` value for the same `issue_number`. |
| 2 | **Source‑ID overlap across tracks without provenance dedup** – Track definitions share `source_ids` (e.g., `SRC-SEC-EDGAR` appears in both ROS‑TRACK‑E and ROS‑TRACK‑I). Correlated data is counted as independent replications. | Inflates perceived reproducibility; violates independence assumption in multi‑track orchestration. | Compute Jaccard overlap of `source_id` sets across all 10 track pairs. If any overlap >20%, require explicit provenance branching (e.g., `source_id:SRC-SEC-EDGAR@v1` vs `@v2`). |
| 3 | **Next‑gate probe external‑dependency non‑determinism** – Probes like `historical_archive_release_date_pit_probe` read live‑archive timestamps. Same candidate yields different gate outcomes if archive metadata shifts between runs. | Same research object passes/fails gate arbitrarily; breaks idempotent reproduction. | Freeze archive snapshot date/ID in probe config; re‑run probe on identical frozen snapshot. Verify output hash is invariant across time. |
